name: King of Damascus
overview: The King of Damascus is a male ruler known primarily for receiving the spoil of Judah from the Arameans, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 24:23. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are provided, making his biblical presence brief but historically significant in the context of Aramean interactions with Judah.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Damascus' literally means 'king [of] Damascus,' indicating his role as the sovereign ruler of the city-state of Damascus. This is a straightforward title without a given divine meaning, simply identifying his political authority as noted in 2 Chronicles 24:23.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Damascus beyond what is indicated by his title and unique attribute. There are no known familial connections or lineage details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Damascus holds significance in the biblical narrative as a figure involved in the conflict surrounding Judah during the period described in 2 Chronicles 24. His receipt of the spoil from the Arameans highlights the geopolitical struggles and incursions affecting Judah at that time. Though his role is limited in Scripture, it reflects the broader historical tensions between Judah and the Aramean powers.
